rows.source_population: Adults with confirmed chronic inflammatory demyelinating polyneuropathy interviewed on symptom experience and immunoglobulin therapy
rows.family_population: 34-year-old adult who had diarrhea 2 weeks ago with worsening weakness in both legs climbing to the thighs over 2 days
rows.note: Direct patient quote ('weakness in my legs') comes from adults with chronic inflammatory demyelinating polyneuropathy rather than acute post-diarrheal ascending inflammatory demyelinating neuropathy.

rows.source_population: Adult patients in China with corneal ulcers (including traumatic mechanical eye injuries such as Participant P2 struck in the eye with bleeding) interviewed on symptom experience
rows.family_population: 37-year-old man struck in the left eye by a tight bungee cord at home today leaving red blood over the lower iris
rows.note: Direct traumatic ocular-impact patient quote ('hit my eye', adapted with unilateral 'left' to 'hit my left eye') comes from a corneal-ulcer cohort participant struck in the eye by a tree branch with bleeding rather than blunt bungee-cord hyphema.

rows.source_population: Adult patients with corneal ulcers interviewed on ocular tearing and symptom experience
rows.family_population: 37-year-old man in the changed-fact control whose left eye started watering mildly for 1 minute at home today
rows.note: Direct ocular-symptom patient quote ('watering') comes from an adult corneal-ulcer cohort describing reflex tearing rather than transient 1-minute benign unilateral eye watering.

rows.expression: and I think it is a skin cut
rows.source_population: Adult eye-trauma patient (Participant P2) in a corneal-ulcer qualitative cohort minimizing traumatic ocular bleeding as a minor skin cut
rows.family_population: 37-year-old man minimizing blunt bungee-cord ocular trauma with blood over the lower iris as a skin cut
rows.note: Same adult traumatic eye-bleeding mechanism where the injured patient minimizes acute ocular trauma with visible bleeding as a minor skin cut ('I thought it was like a skincut'), recast in standard two-word present tense as 'and I think it is a skin cut'.

rows.source_population: Adults with kidney failure and sickle cell disease receiving maintenance dialysis interviewed on lived experience (Participant P1, 46-year-old man on thrice-weekly hemodialysis)
rows.family_population: 68-year-old Black woman on kidney dialysis 3 days a week who felt tired today and had her last session 6 days ago
rows.note: Adult maintenance hemodialysis patient population describing their thrice-weekly schedule verbatim ('dialysis three days a week', normalized to digit '3' per SPEC.md section 4).

rows.source_population: Adults with kidney failure and sickle cell disease receiving maintenance dialysis interviewed on physical fatigue (Participant P3, 58-year-old man on dialysis)
rows.family_population: 68-year-old Black woman on kidney dialysis 3 days a week who felt tired today and had her last session 6 days ago
rows.note: Adult maintenance kidney-failure dialysis patient population describing kidney-failure/dialysis exhaustion verbatim with 'tired'.

rows.source_population: General English speakers (Wiktionary lexical entry 'cuticle', noun sense 2)
rows.family_population: 52-year-old adult with dark brown skin and a lengthwise brown-black stripe under the right thumbnail widening to 5 mm onto the cuticle over 5 months
rows.note: Dictionary entry attests the general English anatomical noun sense ('The strip of hardened skin at the base and sides of a fingernail or toenail.') rather than a longitudinal-melanonychia patient cohort.

rows.source_population: General English speakers (Wiktionary lexical entry 'pimple', noun sense 1)
rows.family_population: 44-year-old man with a pus-draining pimple recurring over 3 weeks on the outer gum below a crowned lower right back tooth
rows.note: Dictionary entry attests the general English noun sense for a small pus-filled raised spot and is applied by extension to a gingival sinus-tract bump on the outer gum rather than a dental patient cohort.

rows.source_population: General English speakers (Wiktionary lexical entry 'spotting', noun sense 3)
rows.family_population: 59-year-old woman with 3 weeks of vaginal blood spotting occurring 6 years after menstrual periods stopped
rows.note: Dictionary entry attests the English lexical sense ('Vaginal spotting, the discharge of blood from the vagina at a time outside of one's usual menses.') rather than a postmenopausal-bleeding patient cohort.

rows.source_population: Postpartum women with postpartum depression synthesized across qualitative interview studies on maternal psychological experiences
rows.family_population: 29-year-old woman 8 weeks after childbirth with 6 weeks of emotional numbness and daily crying persisting after 4 weeks of counseling
rows.note: Same postpartum depression patient population describing frequent tearfulness/crying ('I just want to cry'), inflected to past participle 'cried'.

rows.source_population: General English speakers (Wiktionary lexical entry 'grimace', intransitive verb sense 1)
rows.family_population: Parent describing a 7-year-old boy getting stuck on words with tight jaw grimacing and stretched-out sounds for 8 months when speaking aloud
rows.note: Dictionary entry attests the general English verb sense ('To make grimaces; to distort one's face; to make faces.'), inflected to gerund 'grimacing', rather than a pediatric stuttering carer cohort.

rows.source_population: General English speakers (Wiktionary lexical entry 'clot', noun sense 1)
rows.family_population: 64-year-old man who worked in a dye factory and passed dark red pee with small blood clots 3 times over 2 weeks
rows.note: Dictionary entry attests the general English noun sense ('A thrombus, solidified mass of blood.'), inflected to plural 'clots', rather than a gross-hematuria patient cohort.

rows.source_population: 34 adults in the United States (majority aged 55+ years, 82% male) with non-advanced or advanced basal cell carcinoma interviewed on symptoms
rows.family_population: 63-year-old outdoor worker with an enlarging shiny bump with rolled edges and a scabbed sore on the side of the nose over 7 months
rows.note: Same older male-majority basal cell carcinoma patient population reporting non-healing 'open sores' (41%), inflected to singular 'sore'.

rows.source_population: General English speakers (Wiktionary lexical entry 'scab', noun sense 1)
rows.family_population: 63-year-old outdoor worker with an enlarging shiny bump with rolled edges and a scabbed sore on the side of the nose over 7 months
rows.note: Dictionary entry attests the general English noun sense ('An incrustation over a sore, wound, vesicle, or pustule, formed during healing.'), inflected to 'scabbed', rather than a skin-cancer patient cohort.

rows.source_population: 28 adults in the United States diagnosed with myasthenia gravis completing concept-elicitation interviews
rows.family_population: 46-year-old woman with 6 weeks of evening upper eyelid drooping over both pupils and double vision
rows.note: Same adult myasthenia gravis patient population reporting 'eyelid drooping' (93%) as the most frequent symptom.

rows.source_population: 28 adults in the United States diagnosed with myasthenia gravis completing concept-elicitation interviews
rows.family_population: 46-year-old woman with 6 weeks of evening upper eyelid drooping over both pupils and double vision
rows.note: Same adult myasthenia gravis patient population reporting 'double vision' (43%, within 'blurry/double vision') as the most bothersome symptom.

rows.source_population: Adult hand-surgery / carpal-tunnel patients synthesized in qualitative interviews describing pain when bending the wrist
rows.family_population: 27-year-old adult who carries trays with a 6-week smooth firm 1 cm lump on the back of the right wrist aching mildly when bending the wrist back
rows.note: Direct patient quote ('bend my wrist') comes from adult hand-surgery / carpal-tunnel qualitative interviews rather than a dorsal wrist ganglion cyst cohort.

rows.source_population: Adults with chronic lymphocytic leukemia completing qualitative concept-elicitation surveys on systemic B-symptoms
rows.family_population: 44-year-old man with 6 weeks of 5 kg unintentional weight loss and drenching night sweats soaking bedsheets 4 nights a week
rows.note: Adult hematologic systemic B-symptom population reporting 'night sweats' (38%) verbatim.

rows.source_population: Patients with fingernail and toenail conditions (including ingrown nails) interviewed in NAIL-Q Phase 1 qualitative development
rows.family_population: Parent describing a 14-year-old son wearing sneakers daily whose right big toenail side edge has dug into painful red swollen skin for 9 days
rows.note: Direct patient quote ('I will get an ingrown nail on my finger, and it swells up.', inflected to 'swollen') describes periungual ingrown-fingernail swelling adapted to a teen's ingrown right great toenail fold.

rows.source_population: General English speakers (Wiktionary lexical entry 'wet the bed', verb sense 1)
rows.family_population: Parent describing an 8-year-old daughter previously dry at night since age 5 who has wet the bed during sleep 4 nights a week for 5 weeks
rows.note: Dictionary entry attests the everyday English verbal idiom ('To urinate in one's bed (during sleep).') rather than a pediatric nocturnal-enuresis carer cohort.

rows.source_population: 20 parents/carers and 18 early-childhood educators across 7 childcare centers in Sydney, Australia interviewed on childhood respiratory infections
rows.family_population: Parent describing a 3-year-old daughter in toddler playgroup with 6 days of smelly thick yellow green mucus from only her right nostril
rows.note: Same childcare/playgroup parent population describing young children's colored nasal discharge ('green or yellow', adapted without punctuation to 'yellow green').

rows.source_population: General English speakers (Cambridge Dictionary entry 'gnawing', adjective)
rows.family_population: 48-year-old adult waking at 2 am for 4 weeks with a gnawing hunger ache in the upper middle stomach easing briefly with crackers or milk
rows.note: Dictionary entry attests the general English sensory/pain adjective sense ('continuously uncomfortable, worrying, or painful') rather than an acid-peptic epigastric pain cohort.

rows.source_population: 32 US adults (including 8 MSW) with confirmed Neisseria gonorrhoeae infection completing qualitative concept-elicitation interviews
rows.family_population: 23-year-old man 5 days after a new sexual partner with 2 days of thick yellow discharge from his penis staining underwear and burning urination
rows.note: Same adult male symptomatic urethral STI population reporting penile 'discharge' (4 of 6 symptomatic MSW).
